{{short description|Belgian logician and philosopher (1921–2007)}}
{{Expand French|topic=bio|Jean Ladrière|date=April 2012}}
'''Jean Ladrière''' (September 7, 1921 – November 26, 2007)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.academieroyale.be/n15197/Jean.Ladri%C3%A8re|title=Jean Ladrière|publisher=}}</ref> was a [[Belgium|Belgian]] [[logician]] and [[philosopher]], born in [[Nivelles]]. He was professor at the [[Université catholique de Louvain|University of Louvain]] (UCLouvain)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uclouvain.be/286669.html|title=Fonds Jean Ladrière|first=Thierry|last=Scaillet|date=17 July 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228025622/http://www.uclouvain.be/286669.html|archivedate=28 December 2014}}</ref> from 1959 to 1986, where he was chair of the [[Higher Institute of Philosophy]] from 1977 to 1985.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uclouvain.be/436992.html|title=Biographie|first=Thierry|last=Scaillet|date=24 July 2013|publisher=}}</ref>

The overall project animating his work (650 scientific articles, partially assembled into a dozen volumes) was to develop, in his words, "a report that is not a simple confrontation, but a justified report to the both reflected and lived between the [[Christian faith|(Christian) faith]] and [[reason]]," especially scientific and philosophical reason.

He died in [[Ottignies-Louvain-la-Neuve]].
